examples.en: Getting that angry over so little is really petty.

examples.ko: 밥값 몇천 원을 따지는 건 쪼잔하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it petty to argue over a few thousand won for a meal?
My friend acted so petty that I felt hurt.

examples.ko: 쪼잔한 사람처럼 보이고 싶지 않아서 그냥 냈어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to look petty, so I just paid.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 쪼잔해서 커피 한 잔도 안 사 줘요.
examples.en: Our team leader is so stingy he won't even buy us a coffee.
I guess I was a bit petty back then.

explain: 작은 돈이나 사소한 일에 인색하고 마음이 좁을 때 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. 친구끼리는 농담처럼 쓰지만 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰면 무례해요. 비슷한 말로 '치사하다'가 있고, 반대로 마음이 넓은 사람은 '통이 크다'고 해요.
explain_en: This is a colloquial word for being stingy or small-minded about little money or trivial matters. Friends use it jokingly, but it is rude toward elders or people you just met. A similar word is '치사하다', and the opposite idea is '통이 크다' (to be generous and big-hearted).

examples.ko: 이 떡은 쫄깃쫄깃해서 계속 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: This rice cake is so chewy that I keep eating it.
The chewy noodles go well with the broth.
When I chew the squid slowly, a sweet taste comes out.

examples.ko: 삶은 지 얼마 안 돼서 아직 쫄깃쫄깃해요.
examples.en: It was boiled not long ago, so it is still chewy.

examples.ko: 쫄깃쫄깃하게 구운 닭 껍질이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The chewy grilled chicken skin is the tastiest.
The ramen got soggy, so it isn't chewy.

explain: 부사지만 실제로는 '쫄깃쫄깃하다'나 '쫄깃쫄깃한 면'처럼 더 많이 써요. 면, 오징어, 떡, 고기처럼 탄력 있게 씹히는 음식에 쓰고, 찰기가 강하면 '쫀득쫀득'이라고도 해요. 칭찬하는 말이라 음식 후기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Although it is an adverb, people more often use it as '쫄깃쫄깃하다' or '쫄깃쫄깃한 면'. It describes foods that have a springy chew, like noodles, squid, rice cakes and meat; if it is more sticky and dense, people also say '쫀득쫀득'. It is a compliment, so it appears often in food reviews.

examples.en: Wearing leggings with a long T-shirt is comfortable.
Tight pants are good to wear when exercising.
I bought a new pair of leggings yesterday.
These leggings are so tight that sitting is uncomfortable.
In winter I wear tights under my skirt.

examples.ko: 요즘은 쫄바지 대신 통 넓은 바지가 유행이에요.
examples.en: These days wide-leg pants are in fashion instead of skinny ones.

explain: 몸에 딱 붙는 바지를 편하게 부르는 입말이에요. 패션이나 운동복 이야기에서는 '레깅스'라는 말도 많이 써요. 쫄쫄 붙는 느낌이라 조금 가볍고 장난스러운 말투예요.
explain_en: This is a casual spoken word for pants that cling to the body. In talk about fashion or sportswear, people also use the word '레깅스'. It sounds a little light and playful.

en: going hungry; on an empty stomach

examples.en: I've been starving since morning, so I have no energy.

examples.ko: 점심을 거르고 쫄쫄 굶은 채로 회의했어요.
examples.en: I skipped lunch and sat through the meeting starving.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 쫄쫄 굶으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Going hungry all day is bad for your health.

examples.ko: 쫄쫄 굶고 있는 강아지에게 밥을 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave food to the starving puppy.
I had no money, so I went hungry for two days.
I came without eating anything, so I'll eat a lot.

explain: 거의 '굶다'와 함께 써서 아무것도 못 먹고 계속 배고픈 상태를 나타내요. 같은 소리로 시작하는 '졸졸'(물 흐르는 모양, 따라다니는 모양)과 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with '굶다' to show being hungry for a long time with nothing to eat. Don't confuse it with '졸졸' (a trickling stream, or following closely), which is a different word.

examples.en: If you leave clothes in the washer too long, they get wrinkly.
Grandma's hands are wrinkled, but they are warm.
I flattened the crumpled paper with an iron.
The apple is old, so its skin has shriveled.
I was in the water so long that my fingers are wrinkly.
I threw away the tangerine that had dried up and shriveled.

explain: 마르거나 오그라들어서 주름이 많이 진 모양에 써요. 옷이나 종이가 구겨진 건 '구깃구깃하다'나 '구겨지다'라고도 해요. 사람 피부에는 '주름이 많다'고 말하는 쪽이 부드러워요.
explain_en: It describes something with many wrinkles because it dried out or shrank. For crumpled clothes or paper, people also say '구깃구깃하다' or '구겨지다'. For a person's skin, saying '주름이 많다' sounds gentler.

examples.en: The parcel box arrived crushed.
The car door got dented, so I took it in for repair.
I stepped on the can and it got squashed flat.
A dented pot is inconvenient to use.

examples.ko: 가방 안에서 도시락이 찌그러지지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that the lunchbox doesn't get squashed in your bag.

examples.ko: 공이 찌그러져 있어서 잘 안 굴러가요.
examples.en: The ball is dented, so it doesn't roll well.

explain: 단단한 물건이 눌리거나 부딪혀서 모양이 비뚤어졌을 때 써요. 종이나 옷처럼 부드러운 것이 접히면 '구겨지다'라고 해요. 눌리기 전의 원래 모양이 있다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when a firm object loses its shape because it was pressed or hit. For soft things like paper or clothes that get folded, say '구겨지다' instead. It suggests the thing had a proper shape before it was pressed.

examples.en: In winter I think of the steamed buns sold on the street.

examples.ko: 찐빵 안에 팥이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The steamed bun is full of red bean paste.
My mother steamed buns for us herself.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 찐빵 하나에 우유 한 잔 주세요.
examples.en: One warm steamed bun and a glass of milk, please.

examples.ko: 찐빵이 식으면 딱딱해져서 다시 쪄야 해요.
examples.en: When steamed buns cool they get hard, so you have to steam them again.

examples.ko: 편의점에서 파는 호빵과 찐빵은 뭐가 달라요?
examples.en: What's the difference between the steamed buns sold at convenience stores (hobbang) and jjinppang?

explain: 밀가루 반죽에 보통 팥소를 넣고 찜기에 쪄서 만든 빵이에요. 오븐에 굽는 빵과 달리 촉촉하고 쫀득해서 겨울 간식 느낌이 강해요. '호빵'이라고도 많이 불러요.
explain_en: It is a steamed bun, usually filled with sweet red bean paste, made from wheat dough steamed in a steamer. Unlike baked bread it is moist and soft-chewy, and it feels like a typical winter snack. People also call it '호빵'.

en: apply a hot or cold compress

examples.ko: 목욕탕에서 한 시간 동안 찜질을 했어요.
examples.en: I spent an hour doing a hot compress at the bathhouse.

examples.ko: 허리가 아플 때는 따뜻하게 찜질하면 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: When your back hurts, a warm compress helps.

examples.ko: 뭉친 근육이 풀리게 뜨거운 물수건으로 찜질했어요.
examples.en: I used a hot wet towel as a compress to loosen the tight muscle.
Please put an ice pack on the bruise.
My shoulder was stiff, so I used a hot pack and went to sleep.

examples.ko: 찜질하는 동안 책을 읽으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: If you read a book while using a compress, time passes quickly.

explain: 뜨거운 것을 대면 '온찜질', 차가운 것을 대면 '냉찜질'이에요. '찜질을 하다'로도 자주 말하고, 한국식 사우나 시설은 '찜질방'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Applying something hot is '온찜질' and applying something cold is '냉찜질'. People often say it as '찜질을 하다', and the Korean-style sauna facility is called a '찜질방'.

examples.en: I feel uneasy, as if I forgot something.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말이 계속 찜찜하게 남아요.
examples.en: What that person said keeps nagging at me.
I left the house with an uneasy feeling.

examples.ko: 확실히 끝내지 못해서 찜찜하지만 일단 넘어가요.
examples.en: I couldn't finish it properly and it bothers me, but let's move on for now.

examples.ko: 유통기한이 지난 우유를 마셨더니 찜찜해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I drank milk past its date and feel uneasy, so I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 문을 잠갔는지 기억이 안 나서 찜찜했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't remember if I locked the door, so it bothered me.

explain: 몸이 불쾌하다기보다 마음에 걸려서 개운하지 않은 느낌에 많이 써요. '찝찝하다'도 같은 느낌으로 자주 쓰고, 둘 다 입말에서 흔해요. 해결되지 않은 일이나 의심스러운 상황에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used mostly for a nagging, unsettled feeling in the mind rather than physical discomfort. '찝찝하다' is used in much the same way, and both are common in speech. It fits unresolved matters and doubtful situations well.

examples.ko: 만두를 찜통에 넣고 십 분만 쪄요.
examples.en: Put the dumplings in the steamer and steam them for ten minutes.
Steam is rising from the steamer.

examples.ko: 찜통이 너무 작아서 한 번에 다 못 쪄요.
examples.en: The steamer is too small to steam everything at once.
If there's no water at the bottom of the steamer, it will burn.

examples.ko: 새 찜통을 사서 고구마를 쪄 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought a new steamer and steamed sweet potatoes.

examples.ko: 오늘은 밖에 나가면 찜통 속에 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Going outside today feels like being inside a steamer.

explain: 음식을 찌는 큰 통이에요. 날씨 이야기에서는 푹푹 찌는 더위의 비유로도 많이 나와요. 짝말로 '찜통에 찌다', '찜통에 넣다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This summer the sweltering heat lasted a whole month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찜통 속처럼 습하고 푹푹 찌는 더위를 말해요. 뉴스와 일상에서 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means muggy, steaming heat as if you were inside a steamer. It is used in both the news and daily talk.

explain_en: It is a large pot for steaming food. In weather talk it often appears as a metaphor for oppressive, humid heat. Common pairings are '찜통에 찌다' and '찜통에 넣다'.

examples.en: I dipped my feet into the ice-cold winter sea.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침 바닥이 차디차서 양말을 두 켤레 신었어요.
examples.en: The floor was freezing on the winter morning, so I wore two pairs of socks.

examples.ko: 손이 차디차네요. 이 장갑을 껴 보세요.
examples.en: Your hands are ice cold. Try putting on these gloves.
That person answered coldly and turned away.
The water is freezing, so get in carefully.

examples.ko: 방이 차디차지 않게 보일러를 켜 두었어요.
examples.en: I left the heating on so the room wouldn't be freezing.

explain: '차다'를 강하게 말한 표현이에요. 말할 때는 '엄청 차다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '차디찬' 모양은 글이나 노래 가사에서 자주 보여요. 사람의 냉정한 태도를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a stronger version of '차다' (cold). In speech people more often say '엄청 차다', while the form '차디찬' appears often in writing and song lyrics. It can also describe a cold, unfeeling attitude.

examples.en: I dressed up neatly in a hanbok and took photos.

examples.ko: 내일 면접이라서 정장을 말끔하게 차려입을 거예요.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'll dress up in a neat suit.
Why are you dressed up so nicely today?

examples.ko: 결혼식에 갈 때는 단정하게 차려입는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When going to a wedding, it's good to dress neatly.
I usually dress casually, but I dress up for gatherings.
You look really great all dressed up.

explain: 그냥 '입다'와 달리 격식에 맞게 신경 써서 단정히 입는다는 느낌이에요. '옷을 차려입다'로 쓰고, 멋을 내는 느낌이면 '빼입다'라는 말도 있어요. 평소 옷에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '입다', it suggests putting on clothes carefully and properly for the occasion. It is used as '옷을 차려입다', and there is also '빼입다' for dressing up stylishly. It doesn't fit everyday casual clothes.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 서비스로 다른 곳과 차별화해요.
examples.en: Our shop differentiates itself from others through service.

examples.ko: 어떻게 하면 제품을 차별화할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: How can we differentiate our product?

examples.ko: 경쟁 회사와 차별화하기 위해 디자인을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: We changed the design to set ourselves apart from competitors.
It's hard to stand out on price alone.
Trying hard to be different made things more complicated.
We chose a strategy of differentiating by taste.

explain: 주로 회사, 상품, 서비스를 다른 것과 다르게 만든다는 뜻으로 마케팅이나 업무 대화에서 써요. '차별'은 사람을 부당하게 다르게 대하는 나쁜 뜻이지만 '차별화'에는 그런 느낌이 없어요. '~을 차별화하다'와 '~와 차별화하다'를 둘 다 써요.
explain_en: It is used in business and marketing talk for making a company, product or service different from others. '차별' means treating people unfairly and is negative, but '차별화' has no such feeling. You can say both '~을 차별화하다' and '~와 차별화하다'.

examples.en: There aren't many transport options to that island.
If you arrive late at night, there's no way to get back.

examples.ko: 차편을 미리 알아보고 출발하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to check transport options before you set out.

examples.ko: 시골이라 읍내까지 가는 차편이 하루에 두 번뿐이에요.
examples.en: It's the countryside, so there are only two rides a day to town.

examples.ko: 친구가 차편을 마련해 줘서 편하게 왔어요.
examples.en: A friend arranged a ride for me, so I got here comfortably.

examples.ko: 공연장까지 가는 차편 좀 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to get to the concert hall.

explain: 버스, 기차, 택시처럼 어디로 갈 때 이용할 수 있는 교통수단을 말해요. '있다, 없다, 알아보다, 마련하다'와 잘 어울려요. 같은 뜻으로 '교통편'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the transportation you can use to get somewhere, such as a bus, train or taxi. It pairs well with '있다', '없다', '알아보다' and '마련하다'. '교통편' is also widely used with the same meaning.

examples.en: These shoes are very comfortable to wear.

examples.ko: 마스크 착용감이 불편해서 오래 못 써요.
examples.en: The mask feels uncomfortable, so I can't wear it for long.

examples.ko: 착용감이 가벼워서 하루 종일 껴도 편해요.
examples.en: It feels light, so it's comfortable even if I wear it all day.
How do your new glasses feel to wear?

examples.ko: 이어폰을 살 때는 소리뿐 아니라 착용감도 봐요.
examples.en: When buying earphones, I look at the fit as well as the sound.
At first it felt strange to wear, but I got used to it quickly.

explain: 옷, 신발, 안경, 이어폰, 시계처럼 몸에 걸치거나 끼는 물건의 느낌이에요. 제품 후기에서 '착용감이 좋다/편하다/불편하다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the feel of things you put on your body, such as clothes, shoes, glasses, earphones and watches. In product reviews you often see '착용감이 좋다/편하다/불편하다'.

examples.ko: 컵은 찬장 두 번째 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The cups are on the second shelf of the cupboard.
The cupboard door doesn't close well.
I put the new dishes away in the cupboard.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 찬장에서 과자를 몰래 꺼내 먹었어요.
examples.en: As a child I secretly took snacks out of the cupboard.

examples.ko: 큰 접시는 찬장 위에 올려 놓아요.
examples.en: I put the big plates on top of the cupboard.

examples.ko: 찬장이 좁아서 그릇을 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The cupboard is small, so I can't fit more dishes.

explain: 부엌에서 그릇이나 음식을 넣어 두는 장이에요. 요즘 새 집에서는 '수납장'이라고 하는 경우가 많고, '찬장'은 조금 옛날 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a cabinet in the kitchen for keeping dishes and food. In newer homes people often say '수납장' (storage cabinet), and '찬장' can sound a little old-fashioned.

examples.en: I fell and scraped my knee.
Luckily I only got a light scrape.
I put a bandage on the wound because of the scrape.
It was a bike accident and I got a graze on my arm.

examples.ko: 찰과상은 먼저 깨끗한 물로 씻어 주세요.
examples.en: First wash a scrape with clean water.

examples.ko: 아이가 놀이터에서 놀다가 찰과상을 입고 울었어요.
examples.en: The child scraped herself while playing at the playground and cried.

explain: 스치거나 쓸려서 피부 겉이 벗겨진 얕은 상처예요. 뉴스나 병원에서는 '찰과상'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 '무릎이 까졌어요'처럼 말해요. '찰과상을 입다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a shallow wound where the skin surface is scraped off. In the news and at the hospital people say '찰과상', while in daily life they say things like '무릎이 까졌어요'. A common phrase is '찰과상을 입다'.

examples.en: Ramen and kimchi are a perfect match.
The two of them are a perfect match in personality.

examples.ko: 이 소스와 닭고기는 찰떡궁합이라 자꾸 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: This sauce and chicken go together perfectly, so I keep eating.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 찰떡궁합이라 일이 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: Our team works so well together that the work gets done fast.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 비 오는 날과 찰떡궁합이에요.
examples.en: This song goes perfectly with rainy days.

examples.ko: 둘이 같이 일하면 찰떡궁합을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: When the two work together, they show great chemistry.

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 음식, 물건, 노래와 장면처럼 서로 아주 잘 맞는 것에 두루 써요. '~와 찰떡궁합이다'로 쓰고 말투가 가볍고 친근해서 대화나 방송에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used not only for people but also for foods, objects, songs and scenes that suit each other extremely well. It is used as '~와 찰떡궁합이다', and the tone is light and friendly, so you often hear it in conversation and on TV.

examples.en: Sticky rice is chewier than regular rice.

examples.ko: 어머니가 팥을 넣은 찰밥을 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother made sticky rice with red beans.

examples.ko: 찰밥이 쉽게 굳으니까 따뜻할 때 드세요.
examples.en: Sticky rice hardens easily, so eat it while it's warm.
I wanted sticky rice, so I bought glutinous rice.
I packed sticky rice for my picnic lunch.
Today I ate sticky rice with seasoned vegetable side dishes.

explain: 찹쌀로 지어서 찰기가 센 밥이에요. 보통 쌀로 지은 밥은 그냥 '밥'이라고 해요. '찹쌀밥'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is rice cooked with glutinous rice, so it is very sticky. Rice made from ordinary rice is simply called '밥'. People also say '찹쌀밥'.

examples.en: In summer we steam and eat sticky corn.
Sticky corn is chewy and delicious.
I bought ten ears of sticky corn at the market.
The boiled sticky corn is still warm.
A relative in Gangwon-do sent us sticky corn.
How much is one bag of sticky corn?

explain: 찰기가 있어서 쫀득하게 씹히는 옥수수예요. 여름철 길거리 간식이나 시장 과일가게에서 많이 보여요. 그냥 '옥수수'라고 하면 보통 이 종류만 가리키는 건 아니에요.
explain_en: This is corn with a sticky, chewy texture. It is common as a summer street snack and at market stalls. Plain '옥수수' does not always mean this particular kind.

examples.en: The children made animals out of clay.
Clay gets hard when it dries.
They told us to bring clay to art class.
Clay sticks to my hands and is hard to wash off.

examples.ko: 비닐로 덮어 두면 찰흙이 마르지 않아요.
examples.en: If you cover it with plastic, the clay won't dry out.
I kneaded the clay and shaped it into a bowl.

explain: 학교 미술 시간이나 아이들 공작에서 가장 흔히 듣는 점토 이름이에요. 도자기나 공예 분야에서는 '점토'라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: This is the most common name for clay in school art classes and children's crafts. In ceramics and crafts the word '점토' is also used.

examples.ko: 위기가 닥쳐야 사람의 참모습을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only see a person's true colors when a crisis hits.
When you remove makeup, your real face shows.

examples.ko: 이 사진에서 그 도시의 참모습을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the true face of that city in this photo.

examples.ko: 가까이 지내 보니 그 친구의 참모습이 보였어요.
examples.en: After spending time close to him, I saw my friend's true self.
Don't just look at the surface; look at the real thing.
I was disappointed after learning what he was really like.

explain: 겉으로 보이는 모습과 달리 숨어 있던 진짜 모습을 말해요. '겉모습'과 반대되고, 비슷한 말로 '본모습'이 있어요. 좋은 모습이든 나쁜 모습이든 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means the real appearance that was hidden behind the outward look. It contrasts with '겉모습' (outward appearance), and a similar word is '본모습'. It can be used for either a good or bad true nature.

examples.en: My friend gave me sticky rice cakes the day before the exam.
There is sweet red bean filling inside the rice cake.

examples.ko: 찹쌀떡은 목에 걸리지 않게 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: Eat the rice cake slowly so it doesn't get stuck in your throat.
Rice cakes with strawberry inside are popular.
The rice cake hardened, so I heated it in the microwave.
I ate two rice cakes as a snack.

explain: 찹쌀로 만든 쫀득한 떡이고 속에 팥이나 과일을 넣은 것이 흔해요. 시험 전에 '붙으라'는 뜻으로 찹쌀떡을 선물하는 문화가 있어요. 아주 쫀득하니 목에 걸리지 않게 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: This is a chewy rice cake made from glutinous rice, often filled with red bean paste or fruit. There is a custom of giving it before exams, as a wish that one will 'stick' (pass). It is very sticky, so be careful not to choke.

examples.en: I put the flowerpot on the windowsill.
The cat sits on the windowsill and looks outside.
A lot of dust has piled up on the windowsill.
It rained, so the windowsill is all wet.

examples.ko: 창턱에 놓인 화분에는 고운 모래가 깔려 있어요.
examples.en: Fine sand is spread in the pot on the windowsill.
The windowsill is narrow, so I can't put things on it.

explain: 창문 아래쪽에 가로로 튀어나온 턱이에요. 창문 둘레의 틀은 '창틀', 창문 근처 자리는 '창가'라고 해서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is the ledge that sticks out horizontally at the bottom of a window. The frame around the window is '창틀' and the area near the window is '창가', so they are different words.

examples.en: During the holiday I go to my hometown to visit my parents.
I'll go visit you next week, teacher.

examples.ko: 선생님 댁에 찾아뵈었더니 사모님이 차를 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I visited my teacher's home, his wife served me tea.
I'm sorry I haven't been able to visit you for so long.
At New Year it is polite to visit the elders.

examples.ko: 직접 찾아봬야 하는데 전화로 먼저 인사드려요.
examples.en: I should visit in person, but I'll greet you by phone first.

explain: 윗사람을 만나러 가는 것을 자기를 낮춰서 말하는 표현이라, 부모님, 선생님, 어른께만 써요. '찾아뵙다'도 같은 뜻으로 자주 쓰고, 해요체는 '찾아뵈어요'와 '찾아봬요' 둘 다 가능해요. 친구나 아랫사람에게는 그냥 '찾아가다'를 써요.
explain_en: It humbly describes going to see someone senior, so use it only for parents, teachers and elders. '찾아뵙다' is also commonly used with the same meaning, and the polite form can be either '찾아뵈어요' or '찾아봬요'. For friends or juniors, just use '찾아가다'.

examples.ko: 선생님의 채찍질 덕분에 끝까지 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my teacher's strict push, I studied hard to the end.

examples.ko: 실수했다고 자기 자신을 너무 채찍질하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't be too hard on yourself for making a mistake.
I pushed my lazy mind and sat down at my desk.
Sometimes a sharp push is needed too.
I pushed myself and exercised every day.

examples.ko: 아이를 채찍질만 하면 오히려 공부가 싫어져요.
examples.en: If you only drive a child hard, he ends up hating study.

explain: 원래는 채찍으로 때리는 일이지만 일상에서는 엄하게 몰아붙여 더 노력하게 한다는 비유로 훨씬 많이 써요. '자신을 채찍질하다'처럼 스스로에게 자주 써요. 상대를 몰아붙이는 느낌이면 '다그치다'와 비슷해요.

phrases.example: 더 나은 사람이 되려고 자신을 채찍질했어요.
phrases.en: I pushed myself hard to become a better person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 엄하게 몰아붙여 더 노력하게 한다는 뜻이에요. 격려보다 다그치는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to drive yourself hard so that you try harder. It feels more like pressing yourself than encouraging yourself.

explain_en: Originally it means beating with a whip, but in daily life it is far more often used as a metaphor for strictly driving someone to try harder. It is often used on oneself, as in '자신을 채찍질하다'. When aimed at others it is close to '다그치다' (to press hard).

examples.en: If you slice carrots with a slicer, it's done quickly.
Be careful not to cut your hand on the slicer.

examples.ko: 새로 산 채칼이 아주 잘 들어요.
examples.en: The slicer I just bought cuts really well.
I shredded the cabbage finely with a slicer.
I took out the slicer to make potato pancakes.

examples.ko: 채칼 날을 씻을 때는 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful when washing the slicer blade.

explain: 채소를 가늘고 길게 써는 부엌 도구예요. 가늘게 썬 것을 '채'라고 해서 '채 썰다'라는 말과 이어져요. 갈아서 곱게 가는 도구는 '강판'이라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: It is a kitchen tool for cutting vegetables into thin, long strips. The thin strips are called '채', which links to the phrase '채 썰다'. A tool that grates food finely is a '강판', which is different.

en: backing sheet (placed under paper when writing)

examples.ko: 글씨를 쓸 때 책받침을 대면 편해요.
examples.en: It's easier to write if you put a backing sheet underneath.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 책받침에 만화 캐릭터 그림이 있었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my backing sheet had a cartoon character on it.
Put a backing sheet under your notebook and write.
If I write without a backing sheet, my handwriting gets crooked.
I bought a backing sheet for the new term.

examples.ko: 요즘은 책받침을 쓰는 학생이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many students use backing sheets these days.

explain: 공책 밑에 대고 글씨를 쓰는 얇고 단단한 판이에요. 요즘은 잘 안 써서 옛날 학교 생활을 떠올리게 하는 물건이에요. '깔다'나 '대다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a thin, firm sheet placed under a notebook while writing. Rarely used now, it reminds people of school days in the past. It pairs well with '깔다' and '대다'.

examples.en: I sit cross-legged on the floor and eat.
If I sit cross-legged, my legs go numb.
The children sat in a circle with their legs crossed.
If sitting cross-legged is uncomfortable, sit on a chair.
I watched TV sitting cross-legged.

examples.ko: 명상할 때는 책상다리를 하고 허리를 펴요.
examples.en: When meditating, I sit cross-legged and straighten my back.

explain: 바닥에 앉아 두 다리를 꼬아 앞으로 모으는 자세예요. 보통 '책상다리를 하다'로 쓰고 '양반다리'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the sitting posture on the floor with your legs crossed in front of you. It is usually used as '책상다리를 하다', and people also call it '양반다리'.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to my wife's family home and saw my mother-in-law.
I went on a trip with my wife's family.
My wife's family home is far, so I can't go often.
On holidays I go to my parents' home and then stop by my wife's family.
I moved near my wife's family home and my wife is happy.

examples.ko: 처갓집은 아내가 어릴 때 살던 동네에 있어요.
examples.en: My wife's family home is in the neighborhood where she grew up.

explain: 결혼한 남자가 아내의 부모님 집을 가리킬 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '처가'도 쓰고, 아내가 자기 부모님 집을 말할 때는 '친정', 남편 쪽 집은 '시댁'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A married man uses this for his wife's parents' home. '처가' has the same meaning; a wife calls her own parents' home '친정', and the husband's side is '시댁'.

examples.ko: 처남댁이 직접 담근 김치를 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: My brother-in-law's wife sent me kimchi she made herself.
On the holiday I made jeon together with my brother-in-law's wife.
My brother-in-law's wife is really good at cooking.
I bought a cake to give to my brother-in-law's wife.
My brother-in-law's wife had a baby, so I went to visit her at the hospital.
My brother-in-law and his wife are moving next month.

explain: 결혼한 남자가 아내의 남자 형제의 아내를 부르거나 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요. 아내 쪽 친척에는 '처가', '처형', '처제'처럼 '처-'가 붙는 말이 많아요. 아내 입장에서는 같은 사람을 '올케'라고 해요.
explain_en: A married man uses this to address or refer to the wife of his wife's brother. Many words for his wife's relatives start with '처-', such as '처가', '처형' and '처제'. From the wife's side, the same person is called '올케'.

examples.ko: 그는 처자식을 먹여 살리려고 밤늦게까지 일해요.
examples.en: He works late into the night to support his wife and children.

examples.ko: 처자식을 두고 혼자 해외로 갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go abroad alone and leave my wife and kids.

examples.ko: 아버지는 처자식 생각에 힘든 일도 참으셨어요.
examples.en: My father endured hard work thinking of his wife and children.

examples.ko: 처자식이 있는 가장이라 함부로 직장을 못 그만둬요.
examples.en: He is a breadwinner with a family, so he can't quit his job lightly.

examples.ko: 처자식 걱정은 하지 말고 잘 다녀오세요.
examples.en: Don't worry about your wife and kids, and have a good trip.
My older brother moved to the countryside with his wife and children.

explain: 남자 가장의 입장에서 아내와 자식을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이라 여자에게는 쓰지 않아요. 조금 옛날 느낌과 거친 느낌이 있어서 공손하게 말할 때는 '가족'이라고 하는 쪽이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It lumps a man's wife and children together from the viewpoint of the male head of household, so it is not used about women. It sounds a bit old-fashioned and blunt, so '가족' is more natural when you want to sound polite.

examples.en: My grandmother believes that after death one goes to heaven.
They say if you live a good life, you go to heaven.
Soaking in the hot spring, this feels like heaven.
I heard a story about heaven and hell at church.

examples.ko: 천당에 가려고 착한 일을 하는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: I don't do good deeds in order to go to heaven.
The child asked, 'Where is heaven?'

explain: 종교에서 좋은 사람이 죽은 뒤에 간다고 믿는 곳을 말하고, 반대말은 '지옥'이에요. '천국'이라고도 하고, 일상에서는 아주 편하고 좋은 곳을 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the place religion says good people go after death, and its opposite is '지옥' (hell). People also say '천국', and in daily talk it can be a metaphor for a very comfortable, pleasant place.

examples.ko: 풍부한 천연자원 덕분에 이 나라는 부자예요.
examples.en: Thanks to its rich natural resources, this country is wealthy.
Countries short of natural resources depend on imports.
Oil is a typical natural resource.
We need the habit of using natural resources sparingly.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 천연자원이 거의 없어서 기술로 먹고살아요.
examples.en: Our country has almost no natural resources, so it lives by technology.

examples.ko: 천연자원 개발 때문에 숲이 줄어들고 있어요.
examples.en: Forests are shrinking because of the development of natural resources.

explain: 석유, 석탄, 철, 물, 숲처럼 자연에서 얻는 자원이에요. 뉴스, 사회 수업, 경제 이야기에 자주 나와요. 사람의 능력을 자원으로 말하는 '인적 자원'과 짝으로 기억해 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: These are resources taken from nature, such as oil, coal, iron, water and forests. They come up often in the news, social studies and economics. It helps to remember it as a pair with '인적 자원' (human resources), which treats people's abilities as a resource.

examples.en: The train crosses the iron bridge slowly.
A train passes over the Han River railway bridge.

examples.ko: 오래된 철교가 낡아서 새로 놓기로 했어요.
examples.en: The old iron bridge is worn out, so they decided to build a new one.
Many people fish under the iron bridge.

examples.ko: 철교를 건널 때 창밖 경치가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The view out the window was beautiful as we crossed the bridge.
It's dangerous to take photos on a railway bridge.

explain: 쇠로 만든 다리이고, 실제로는 기차나 지하철이 다니는 다리를 가리킬 때가 많아요. 자동차가 다니는 일반 다리는 보통 그냥 '다리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a bridge made of iron, and in practice it often refers to a bridge that trains or subways run over. An ordinary bridge for cars is usually just called '다리'.

examples.ko: 이 도로는 철길과 나란히 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: This road runs alongside the railroad tracks.

examples.ko: 철길을 건널 때는 기차가 오는지 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When crossing the tracks, be sure to check whether a train is coming.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 철길이 있어서 기차 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: There are tracks in front of my house, so train noise is loud.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 철길 옆에서 놀다가 혼난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: As a child I once got scolded for playing next to the tracks.
The old railroad has been turned into a walking path.

examples.ko: 철길 위로 올라가면 위험하니까 가지 마세요.
examples.en: It's dangerous to go onto the tracks, so don't.

explain: 기차가 다니는 길이에요. '철로'도 비슷한데 '철길'이 일상 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요. 같은 뜻으로 '기찻길'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the way trains run on. '철로' is similar, but '철길' sounds softer in everyday conversation. '기찻길' is also widely used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I guess our son has finally grown up.
When will my younger sibling grow up?
I only matured after getting married.
When you grow up, you come to understand your parents' hearts.
She looks after her younger sibling like a mature child.

examples.ko: 나이만 먹고 철들지 않는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people get older but never mature.

explain: 나이를 먹으면서 세상 이치와 남의 마음을 알고 어른스러워진다는 느낌이에요. '철이 들다'라고도 하고, 반대는 '철이 없다'나 '철부지'예요. 쇠를 뜻하는 '철'과는 관계없는 말이에요.
explain_en: It gives the sense of growing up and coming to understand how the world works and how others feel. People also say '철이 들다', and the opposites are '철이 없다' and '철부지'. This '철' is unrelated to the '철' that means iron.
